terms.gloss: one who has fled home or country, a refugee
terms.grammar: the adjective profugus, profuga, profugum, used as a noun
evidence: Sall. C. 6.1: Trojānī, quī Aenēā duce profugī sēdibus incertīs vagābantur
terms.comment: In prose an adjective, “fled”, with the place in the ablative (profugus domō, Liv. 1.1); as a noun chiefly in verse and comedy (Plaut. Trin. 3.2.75, Ov.). Not in Cicero or Caesar (Lewis & Short). Morgan–Owens and Egger give it for the modern refugee.

evidence: Cic. de Or. 2.75: Ephesum ad Antiochum vēnisset exsul (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: One sent away from home by law or by force; a refugee who chose to flee is rather profugus.
Not a refugee: one who goes over to the other side (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: Trojānī, quī Aenēā duce profugī sēdibus incertīs vagābantur
phrases.english: the Trojans, who under Aeneas’ leadership were wandering as refugees, with no settled home

sources: Lewis & Short: profugus · Lewis & Short: exsul · Lewis & Short: perfuga
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. refugee.
Sallust, Catilina 6.1, checked against the Perseus Latin texts.
